claims.text: An adaptively refined machine-learning potential trained on solid- and liquid-phase AIMD data near melting will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The adaptive machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to static EAM references used in TOR-TILD.
The principal target composition is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Fe–Ni and Co–Cr are proposed as binary subsystems for testing the method.
The machine-learning potential will be trained on AIMD trajectories and refined through adaptive sampling of underrepresented high-energy liquid configurations.
The proposed simulations cover approximately 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm.
Both NVE and NPT ensembles will be used to sample high-temperature solid, liquid, and solid–liquid coexistence configurations.
The learned potential-energy surface will represent many-body interactions and local atomic environments.
The potential-energy surface will be updated through adaptive reweighting based on discrepancies between AIMD data and potential predictions.
Active learning can identify poorly sampled regions of the ab initio configuration space.
Adding configurations from poorly sampled regions to the training set will systematically reduce errors relative to AIMD.
The refined potential will better reproduce complex local bond rearrangements in the high-temperature liquid.
The refined potential will better reproduce long-range correlations in the high-temperature liquid.
Better reproduction of liquid configurations will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is predicted to decrease by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD using static EAM references.
The adaptive potential is predicted to bring the latent heat of melting within the uncertainty limits of an AIMD benchmark.
The adaptive potential is predicted to bring the free-energy barrier associated with undercooling within the uncertainty limits of an AIMD benchmark.
Static EAM references tend to underrepresent the combinatorial complexity of disordered liquid configurations in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method is expected to apply to CoCrFeMnNi, similar multicomponent alloys, and selected binaries over approximately 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm.
